title: Why Does a Swing Come Back? Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A ball rolls down a slope and up the other side. A child on a slide speeds up on the way down. Speed comes and goes, so where does it go, and how does it come back? Diya pulls her little cousin's swing back and lets go: it speeds up, slows down, stops for a moment and comes back, and nobody pushes it. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE Main and NEET, we learn the conservation of mechanical energy.

A 20 kg child on a 2.5 m swing is let go at 60 degrees in a live simulation that moves like a real pendulum. The readout shows U = 245 J at the top turning into K = 245 J at the bottom, while the graph of K, U and E against the angle keeps E as a flat line. A slow-mo replay shows why the rope does no work. We prove K + U = constant from the work-energy theorem step by step, find v = √(2gh) link by link, compare a child and an adult on the same swing, and see where a real swing's energy goes. Then a worked example with a ball thrown from a balcony, the exam trap about friction, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
